Tom — thanks for the data, that trend makes sense. I pulled a few options that map to how other logistics customers have handled similar growth:

Option A — 12M Price-Hold (Simple)
- 12-month fixed unit rate on committed usage
- ~15% discount off list for a 6-month-rolling commit (example: commit = current baseline * 1.5)
- No burst credits (bursts billed at pay-as-you-go)

Option B — Commit-Flex + Surge Buffer (Recommended)
- Commit for 12 months with quarterly true-ups. Baseline commit = projected steady-state (we can use your 6-month moving avg)
- Price hold on committed units for 12 months at a 20% discount off list if you sign a 12M commit
- Surge buffer: pre-funded credit pool (one-time top-up) that automatically applies to bursts above commit; buffer size is configurable and can be replenished monthly. Burst consumption billed against buffer at a pre-agreed unit rate (example $0.0009/token for burst window)
- Guaranteed priority lanes for burst requests up to configured burst QPS (subject to regional capacity SLO)

Option C — Dynamic Hybrid
- Lower commit discount, larger burst pool, automatic fallback to cheaper model variants outside peak windows

I attached a short proposal (Redwood-Commit-Proposal-v3.pdf) showing numeric examples against your CSV.

Next steps: can you confirm whether procurement needs an explicit SLA for burst availability and whether auto-replenishment of the buffer is acceptable? If yes, I’ll loop in Lauren from Renewals/legal and Ava from SE to iron out the technical and contractual details.

—Michael

Hi all — quick technical note on burst buffer behavior so procurement can map to SOW: 

- Surge buffer is a pre-funded credit bucket (designated to your account). Credits are consumed only when usage exceeds the committed baseline for the billing period.
- Buffer expiry: configurable. Typical setup: monthly top-up + 90-day rollover for unused credits, or set to expire at month-end if you prefer clean accounting.
- Availability guarantee: we commit to a regional burst allocation (example: up to 30% above committed QPS for sustained 15-minute windows) with automatic fallback to a best-effort lane if regional GPUs are saturated. That fallback has a documented lat/throughput profile.
- Billing inside buffer: we can lock a unit price for buffer consumption (example in proposal: $0.0009/token). Pay-as-you-go when buffer is exhausted will be at the standard overage rate unless you opt for auto-replenish.

If you want, I’ll add a short SLA paragraph with the exact quantiles and fallback behavior to the SOW.

–Ava
